items.summary: Project Cedar: Atlas approval reliability
items.description:
Project Cedar improves the reliability and auditability of Atlas approval workflows.

- Executive sponsor: Priya Shah
- Delivery lead: Theo Park
- Approved envelope: $48,000

## Release gates

- Passing approval-path regression tests
- No open tenant-isolation finding
- An accepted rollback drill
- Joint Engineering and IT Operations readiness approval

Source of truth for status is the latest steering snapshot (ACME-023), not this epic.
comments: Sept 4 snapshot: Cedar is amber. Rollout forecast moved from September 15 to September 22, 2026; Priya approved the revised forecast at the September 3 steering meeting.

items.summary: Tenant-scoped idempotency key for approval notifications
items.description:
Implement the tenant-scoped idempotent delivery decision from ADR-001 so a retried approval event cannot notify the same approver twice.

Follow-up to INC-2026-02 (duplicate approval notifications).

## Acceptance

- The idempotency key includes the tenant identifier
- Component review passed
comments: Component review passed. Retry regression evidence is tracked separately in the Cedar retry regression task.

items.summary: Clearer approval-history view
items.description: Give workflow administrators a clearer approval-history view. Customer-facing workflow rules must remain backward compatible.
comments: Approval-history interface passed its component review. Three pilot workspaces completed the basic approval path.

items.summary: Retry regression evidence for duplicate notification delivery
items.description:
Owner: Theo Park

Produce regression evidence that retried deliveries do not send duplicate approval notifications. This is a Cedar release gate and must close before the joint Engineering and IT Operations readiness decision.
comments: Two of the three planned retry scenarios pass in staging. The third, a retry after a partial tenant failover, still needs a test fixture. Theo Park
Reminder: a passing component review is not the same as this regression gate. Keep them separate in the steering report.

items.summary: Rollback drill sign-off after restore credential issue
items.description:
Owner: Morgan Reed
Reviewer: Jordan Blake

The August 27 restore drill took 95 minutes against a 60-minute target because the runbook referenced an obsolete credential location (INC-2026-04).

- Update the runbook to use the managed secret alias
- Validate that the incident role can resolve it
- Repeat the drill and record the measured restore time
comments: Runbook updated to the managed secret alias. Repeat drill not yet scheduled; an assigned due date is not proof the repeat test succeeded. Morgan Reed

items.summary: Joint Engineering and IT Operations readiness decision
items.description: Record the joint readiness decision for the Cedar rollout. Blocked until the retry regression evidence and the rollback drill sign-off are accepted.

items.summary: Revised pilot update for Cedar pilot workspaces
items.description: Customer Success prepares a revised update for the three Cedar pilot workspaces reflecting the September 22 forecast. Do not describe a customer-wide launch; none has been recorded.

items.summary: Project Aurora: Beacon regional reporting
items.description:
Project Aurora adds regional reporting to Beacon.

- Sponsor: Priya Shah
- Delivery lead: Leo Martin
- Planning envelope: $32,000
- Limited pilot target: October 6, 2026

No general-availability date has been approved. Until the exit gates close, sales material must describe Aurora as a planned pilot.

items.summary: Validate region tags in a non-production dataset
items.description:
Owner: Leo Martin

Stage one of the Aurora rollout. Customer data must not be copied into test fixtures to accelerate this check.
comments: Region tags validated for synthetic North America data. European records are waiting on the hosting-region decision. Leo Martin

items.summary: Compare regional aggregate totals with the existing report
items.description: Stage two of the Aurora rollout: compare aggregate totals from the regional report with the existing Beacon report before inviting pilot customers.

items.summary: Reconcile Beacon guide retention with the data retention standard
items.description:
Owner: Leo Martin
Reviewer: Jordan Blake

The controlled Data Retention Standard v2 says audit records are kept 365 days. The draft Beacon administration guide says 180 days. The standard is the authority; update the guide and confirm the implementation matches.
comments: Implementation confirmed at 365 days. Guide update drafted and waiting on Jordan Blake's review.

items.summary: Decide hosting region for European customer data
items.description:
ADR-005 (Beacon regional storage) is still pending. No signed data-residency architecture exists.

A meeting attendee's preference for a region is not an approved hosting commitment.
comments: Blocks European region tagging and the pilot exit gate.

items.summary: Customer communication plan for the Aurora pilot
items.description: One of the three Aurora pilot exit gates, alongside the region decision and retention evidence.

items.summary: Project Ledger: vendor reference cleanup
items.description:
Project Ledger cleans vendor reference data in ProcureFlow and reconciles it with LedgerOne.

- Lead: Ravi Desai
- Sponsor: Elena Ortiz
- Envelope: $12,000

No automatic production merges are authorized. Never store bank-account data in the knowledge base.

items.summary: Staging report normalizing vendor names and tax-reference placeholders
items.description:
Build the staging report that normalizes vendor names and tax-reference placeholders.

Baseline inventory: 240 vendor records and 36 possible duplicate pairs. These are candidate pairs, not 36 confirmed duplicate vendors.

items.summary: Finance review of candidate duplicate vendor pairs
items.description:
Owner: Ravi Desai

Finance records a decision for every candidate pair. Keep the surviving identifier, source identifiers, reviewer, and reason in the merge log.
comments: A declined merge counts as reviewed, not as an unresolved failure. There is no target to force the vendor count down.

items.summary: Sample ten purchase orders after approved merges
items.description: Acceptance check: a sample of ten purchase orders must resolve to the intended vendor, and historical purchase-order references must remain resolvable.

items.summary: Confirm the Nimbus renewal uses the reviewed vendor record
items.description: The Nimbus compute renewal must use the reviewed vendor record before any commitment.

items.summary: Project Compass: standard customer onboarding
items.description:
Compass standardizes customer onboarding across Atlas and Harbor.

- Sponsor and lead: Samira Cole
- Envelope: $8,000
- Pilot account: Pinecrest Services (fictional)

Target: an accepted handoff within ten business days after all customer prerequisites are complete.

items.summary: Kickoff checklist for the Pinecrest Services pilot
items.description: Kickoff checklist covering the prerequisites: a signed scope, a named customer administrator, approved test data, and validated access.

items.summary: Responsibility map and configuration record
items.description:
Owner: Samira Cole

Deliver the responsibility map and configuration record for the Pinecrest pilot.
comments: Pinecrest's named administrator is confirmed; approved test data is still outstanding, so the ten-day clock has not started. Samira Cole

items.summary: Onboarding tracker starts the handoff clock at the sales introduction
items.description:
The onboarding tracker starts the ten-business-day handoff clock when sales makes the first introduction. Per the Compass plan, the clock starts only once all customer prerequisites are complete; an informal sales introduction or unsigned proposal does not start it.

## Expected

- Clock starts when the last prerequisite is marked complete
- Missing prerequisites are reported separately from execution delays
